co-arapahoe-2026-treasurer-westerberg-mi.name: Michael Westerberg
co-arapahoe-2026-treasurer-westerberg-mi.bio: Arapahoe County Treasurer and tax attorney with a Master of Laws in Taxation from the University of Denver.

positions.stance: Wants a more efficient Treasurer's Office, including improved procedures, living wages for staff, and updated technology so residents can access services easily.
Wants "every penny to be invested every minute it's in the county's possession" and benchmarks county investment returns against CSAFE and ColoTrust.
Aims to make paying property taxes online easier and more secure to collect more taxes before the annual tax lien sale.
Says Arapahoe County could support a public bank and is developing a plan to offer loans for small businesses and affordable housing.

co-arapahoe-2026-assessor-kaiser-pk.name: PK Kaiser
co-arapahoe-2026-assessor-kaiser-pk.bio: Arapahoe County Assessor since 2018; former State of Colorado tax examiner and USPS real estate manager.

positions.stance: Streamlining applications for the Senior Property Tax Exemption and Disabled Veteran Exemption so eligible residents receive every exemption they are entitled to.
Using advanced data analytics so property valuations are accurate, consistent, and reflect true market conditions across all neighborhoods.
Plans a fully digital transparency portal letting residents track assessment cycles and funding allocations in real time.

co-arapahoe-2026-assessor-lind-jesse.name: Jesse Lind
co-arapahoe-2026-assessor-lind-jesse.bio: Software engineer and operations leader; Army veteran and former Denver paramedic.

positions.stance: "You should know where every single cent of your tax bill is going and which authority is responsible."
The burden of proof in a valuation appeal should rest on the county once the owner makes a good-faith case; appraisers must show their work.
"Fraud, waste, or abuse should be assumed until proven otherwise whenever anyone cannot easily follow the money."
Every valuation step should be public, auditable, and understandable without appraisal experience.
Comparable sales should be mailed to owners, remain available for every year, and be understandable without appraisal experience.

co-arapahoe-2026-sheriff-brown-tyler.name: Tyler Scott Brown
co-arapahoe-2026-sheriff-brown-tyler.bio: Arapahoe County Sheriff since 2019; former police officer in Northglenn and Mountain View.

positions.stance: Wants to continue expanding mental health tools and resources in both public safety and the detention facility.
Plans to fully deploy body-worn cameras on all deputies, including in the courts and detention facility.
Wants a diversion program with the District Attorney's Office to move low-level offenders into treatment and reduce recidivism.
Starting a detention facility program for real-time biometric monitoring of the health and vitals of people in custody.
Plans to integrate new technologies, including stationary FLOCK camera systems throughout the county, to help reduce crime.

co-arapahoe-2026-sheriff-edling-kevin.name: Kevin Scott Edling
co-arapahoe-2026-sheriff-edling-kevin.bio: Retired Denver Police Department command officer and Colorado Air National Guard veteran.

positions.stance: "Real law enforcement-fair, firm, and fearless"; would mirror the Aurora Police Department's vehicle chase policy.
Aims to decrease property crimes through proactive policing strategies.
Prioritizes providing excellent customer service to residents.
Prioritizes "delivering accountable, responsible leadership."

co-jefferson-2026-commissioner-d3-cutter.name: Lisa A. Cutter
co-jefferson-2026-commissioner-d3-cutter.bio: Colorado state legislator and founder of the public relations firm Cutter Communications.

positions.stance: Says the economy must work for everyone and supports safeguards against profiteering and price-gouging and a balanced tax structure.
"Quality health care shouldn't be a luxury – access for all is a basic right"; supports price transparency and controls on unwarranted markups.
Supports equal pay, affordable childcare, and protecting reproductive rights, saying these medical decisions belong to patients, families, and doctors.
"Mental health is health. Period." Supports insurance parity between mental and medical health treatment and the behavioral health workforce.
Supports veterans, seniors, BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and disabled people, and says Colorado should not tolerate racism, bigotry or hatred.

co-jefferson-2026-clerk-hensel-nicole.name: Nicole Hensel
co-jefferson-2026-clerk-hensel-nicole.bio: Former teacher, organizer, and nonprofit leader.

positions.stance: Wants every eligible voter registered and able to vote, closing turnout gaps for voters of color, working-class voters, and young voters.
Will run elections, motor vehicles, recording, licenses, and passports efficiently and innovate how the office delivers services.
Would explore fostering deeper connections between Jefferson County elected officials and constituents to build trust.

co-jefferson-2026-treasurer-proctor-eric.name: Eric Proctor
co-jefferson-2026-treasurer-proctor-eric.bio: Community banker for the last twelve years.

positions.stance: Will work with local financial institutions to prioritize access to capital for all, while earning a solid return on taxpayer funds.
Says citizens should be informed how their funds are invested and the office should invest with partners who share county values.
Financial institutions holding public funds should be accountable and should not assume those funds will always remain with them.

co-jefferson-2026-assessor-kerr-andy.name: Andy Kerr
co-jefferson-2026-assessor-kerr-andy.bio: Jefferson County Commissioner; former state senator and Jeffco middle school social studies teacher.

positions.stance: Supports a paid sick leave standard, living wages for county employees, prevailing wages on public contracts, and closing corporate tax loopholes.
Will work with state and local leaders toward universal pre-K for all families in Jefferson County.
Will push to expand multi-use trails, outdoor education, wildfire mitigation support, and the conservation easement program.
Wants better road maintenance and says Jefferson County should lead on multimodal transportation, including first- and last-mile links.
Supports the goals of the 2018 Jeffco Comprehensive Plan to balance preserving Jeffco's character with welcoming newcomers.

co-jefferson-2026-sheriff-doizaki-randal.name: Randall Doizaki
co-jefferson-2026-sheriff-doizaki-randal.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran and retired Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office lieutenant.

positions.stance: Supports proactive policing and crime prevention, focusing resources on violent crime and repeat offenders, and emergency preparedness.
Wants to develop future leaders, improve recruitment and retention, expand training, and strengthen employee wellness and peer support.
Wants to increase transparency, improve communication with residents, and expand community engagement and partnerships.
Emphasizes clear expectations, ethical leadership, responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources, and data-informed decision making.

ut-utah-2026-clerk-astill-corey.name: Corey K Astill
ut-utah-2026-clerk-astill-corey.bio: Former Vice-President of the Business Roundtable and former U.S. Senate legislative aide.

positions.stance: Says the Clerk should prioritize election integrity "without injecting personal agendas or creating unnecessary barriers for voters."
Pledges professional management, strong internal controls, transparent operations, and clear communication with voters from day one.

ut-utah-2026-sheriff-smith-mike.name: Mike Smith
ut-utah-2026-sheriff-smith-mike.bio: Utah County Sheriff since 2018, now in his second term; former Pleasant Grove Chief of Police.

ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-robinson-julius.name: Julius Robinson
ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-robinson-julius.bio: Former executive vice president of community reinvestment (CRA) at Union Bank/MUFG.

positions.stance: Supports full police staffing to the Measure NN minimum of 700 officers, sustained violence-prevention funding, and faster 911 response.
Wants to expand capital for small, minority, and women-owned businesses and launch an Oakland Opportunity Fund.
Supports down payment assistance, protecting affordable housing and tenants from displacement, and partnering to build housing faster.
Wants to end illegal dumping, speed cleanup in every neighborhood, and maintain parks and sidewalks to one citywide standard.
Proposes a 100-day fiscal transparency plan with department scorecards, spending dashboards, and independent audits of major contracts.

ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-lee-barbara.name: Barbara Lee
ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-lee-barbara.bio: Mayor of Oakland since 2025; former U.S. Representative and California state legislator.

positions.stance: Prioritizes preventing homelessness, connecting people to services, clearing encampments, providing shelter, and building more affordable housing.
Wants neighborhoods hit hardest by illegal dumping to get focused attention and long-term solutions.
Will escalate cross-department wildfire operations and keep fire stations open and operational.
Will "continue to advance a comprehensive, community-focused approach to public safety."
Plans to finalize and present a Charter Reform vision for voters to consider.

ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-grisham-brenda.name: Brenda F. Grisham
ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-grisham-brenda.bio: Community advocate, business owner, and victims' rights advocate.

positions.stance: Calls for safer neighborhoods and stronger public safety.
Calls for accountability and transparency in city government.
Supports economic growth that supports local businesses.
Supports housing stability for Oakland families.
Calls for cleaner streets and stronger city services.

ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-pechenuk-mindy.name: Mindy Ruth Pechenuk
ca-alameda-2026-oakmayor-pechenuk-mindy.bio: Musician and educator with a Bachelor of Music from Queens College and decades of community organizing and political activism.

positions.stance: Proposes growing the police department to 1,000 officers, ending federal oversight, and replacing the MACRO program with treatment centers.
Proposes a drug task force with DEA and CHP to target dealers, raid illegal cannabis warehouses, and clear open-air drug markets.
Proposes restructuring city debt, a full outside audit including nonprofits, and tax incentives for small businesses and manufacturing.
Would work with agencies to fund classes for struggling students, expand arts and science, and create more trade schools.
Supports immediate rehabilitation for people with addiction or mental illness and job offers for unemployed or homeless citizens.
